title: The Feature List keys every feature on one of 19 modules, and 13 of the module names differ from the Arch v5 service names
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, Features sheet columns B and C; Microservice Ownership Map v1, Services sheet; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Template and Rules R4 and R5.1
section: Features columns B, C, O and P; By module columns A, B, H and I; Key sheet Module and Column rows
description: The workbook organises all 378 features by a two-letter module code (P1 to P10 and S1 to S9) and a module name of its own; it has no service column and no service-epic column. Architecture v5 says recovery-core is split into 19 services, one per business module, and the Ownership Map names each one with a code, a short name, a schema, a wave and an epic. The code maps one to one, but 13 module names differ from the service names: P1 Recovery data engine, P4 Access and administration, P5 Document hub, P7 Decision center and log, P8 Payments and posting, P10 Agent runtime, S2 TDR settlement and deed in lieu, S3 Guarantees and guarantors, S4 Litigation and enforcement, S5 Assets and auction, S7 Write-off and recovery, S8 Deviation handling and S9 Partner management. Six are the same: P2, P3, P6, P9, S1 and S6. Nothing in the source says which of the two names is authoritative, and nothing in the source gives a service epic for a feature.
evidence: Features row 4 has 14 columns and no Service column; By module row 4 has 7 columns and no Service column. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 18: 'recovery-core is split further into 19 services, one per business module, so each can be repurposed later'. Line 2713: 'one deployable and one schema become 19 services with a schema and login each in the same ACE database'. Ownership Map v1 Services sheet: 19 rows, code, service short name, name, wave, schema, REST base, topic, queue.
legacy_ref: None (the Module column carries no legacy story key)
owner_role: Business architect and the platform solution architect
proposed: Read the module code as the service code and keep the module names as the workbook's own labels; take Service and Service epic from the Ownership Map, in the form 'P1 rwb-source-data' and 'RWB-SVC-P1'; do not rename a module in v5. A later version that wants one name per service takes the Architecture v5 catalogue as its source and raises the renaming as a documentation change.

title: FEAT-RDF-01 still creates one recovery schema of 92 tables while D-RCV-60 gives each service its own schema
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-RDF-01 and FEAT-RDF-25; Template and Rules R6 and R5.5 DP-01; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2713
section: Features rows FEAT-RDF-01 and FEAT-RDF-25, columns E, F and J
description: FEAT-RDF-01 delivers 'the recovery schema in the ACE database: 92 tables, including the 4 extension tables, and the two migrations that carry the ACE source views'. FEAT-RDF-25 builds, grants and tests the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views. Under D-RCV-60 the built migration is kept but the single schema is split into one schema per service in the same ACE database (rwb_source_data to rwb_partner), one login each, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables. The split is new work (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB stories) and R6 records it in the Change Register; the two feature rows still describe the built position as the delivery.
evidence: FEAT-RDF-01 text: 'Creates the recovery schema in the ACE database: 92 tables, including the 4 extension tables, and the two migrations that carry the ACE source views.' FEAT-RDF-01 systems: 'ACE database, Workbench'. Template and Rules R6, row 'Must change': 'In build: the single recovery schema (92 tables, 14 data products, dictionary). The built migration is kept. The split into rwb_* schemas is new work (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB stories).' DP-01: 'Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables'. Architecture v5 line 2713: '19 services with a schema and login each in the same ACE database'.
owner_role: ACE database team lead and the platform DB solution architect
proposed: Keep both feature rows word for word and build the split as the platform DB story and the 19 per-service DB stories, each in its own schema with its own Flyway sequence. Do not change the 92-table count or the 30-view count in v5; the Change Register carries the split.

title: Ten interaction-ledger features are listed in module P7 while the Ownership Map and DP-18 place the ledger with P1 rwb-source-data
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10; Template and Rules R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-18; Microservice Ownership Map v1, Tables and Rulings sheets
section: Features rows FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10, columns B, E and J; Features columns O and P
description: All ten ledger features carry module P7: write every Workbench event to the ledger, hold the ledger beside the decision log, read it in one ordered sequence, reject a duplicate entry, raise an incident when it cannot be written, bring contact, dispatch and hand-over outcomes in, read the timeline on the case, and set the retention class. The R3 default ruling gives the interaction ledger to P1 rwb-source-data, DP-18 makes P1 the ledger owner, and the Ownership Map gives interaction and efs_ledger_outcome to P1 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-1, which keeps the case timeline and the interaction API with P3. FEAT-ILG-10 also touches retention, which the map gives to P5 rwb-document (retention_rule, ASM-A6-tables-10). The workbook has no owner column, so v5 cannot show the split; it keeps the module label and the Service column follows the module rule of CG-B-BIZ-36-1.
evidence: FEAT-ILG-02: 'Hold the ledger beside the decision log', systems 'Workbench, ACE database', module P7, story keys N5. FEAT-ILG-06, 07 and 08 bring contact, dispatch and hand-over outcomes in (story key N4). Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: interaction owner P1, efs_ledger_outcome owner P1, both with ruling ASM-A6-tables-1. Template and Rules R3 default ruling table: 'Interaction ledger | P1 rwb-source-data'. DP-18: 'Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling)'.
owner_role: Solution architect of P1 rwb-source-data and of P7 rwb-decision
proposed: Keep the ten features in P7 as the module that lists them and keep the Service column at P7 under the module rule. At story stage the ledger write, the store and the intake rule become P1 work through its contract and DP-18; the timeline on the case and the interaction API become P3 work; the retention class is applied through P5's retention contract. The Service Story Catalog records the split.

title: Three live features carry story key A14, whose legacy story RWB-E1-014 D-RCV-60 retires with no new story
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-RDF-20, FEAT-DRI-06 and FEAT-RPT-04; Template and Rules R6 (retired) and R5.5 DP-17; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 2043, 2701 and 2920
section: Features rows FEAT-RDF-20, FEAT-DRI-06 and FEAT-RPT-04, columns E, J, K and M
description: FEAT-RDF-20 copies the decision log to the lake, FEAT-DRI-06 streams the decision log to the data lake, and FEAT-RPT-04 publishes operations reporting from the decision log; all three carry story key A14 and are listed as live System class features of epic E1 and E2. R6 retires RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake: no data lake in Arch v5) with no new story, and DP-17 removes the data lake, with reporting read from events into rwb-reporting. In the target, each service writes a local decision record and publishes DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1, rwb-decision consumes it into the central ledger within five minutes, and rwb-reporting builds its read model from the events.
evidence: FEAT-RDF-20: 'Copy the decision log to the lake', systems 'Data lake', story key A14. FEAT-DRI-06: 'Stream the decision log to the data lake', systems 'Data lake', story key A14. FEAT-RPT-04: 'Publish operations reporting from the decision log', systems 'Power BI, Data lake', story key A14. R6: 'Retired | RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake: no data lake in Arch v5) ... No new story. Dependencies on E1-014 are dropped.' Architecture v5 line 2920: '08 | DecisionRecorded | all 19 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | rwb-decision, rwb-reporting'. Line 2043: local record plus DecisionRecorded through the outbox, central ledger in rwb-decision within five minutes.
owner_role: Solution architect of P7 rwb-decision and the reporting lead of P9 rwb-reporting
proposed: Keep all three rows unchanged in v5 and do not build them. The local decision record plus the central ledger (DP-03, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) replaces the lake copy, and rwb-reporting reads DecisionRecorded. Record the retirement at story stage in the Change Register; the dependency from any story on E1-014 is dropped.

title: Seven live features name the Data lake and Power BI as their systems, and INT-19 and INT-20 are removed
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-RDF-12, FEAT-RDF-19, FEAT-OCC-12, FEAT-RPT-01, FEAT-RPT-05, FEAT-RPT-07 and FEAT-RPT-08; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 707, 2701 and 2703
section: Features rows FEAT-RDF-12, FEAT-RDF-19, FEAT-OCC-12, FEAT-RPT-01, FEAT-RPT-05, FEAT-RPT-07 and FEAT-RPT-08, column J
description: Seven live features publish into the data lake and Power BI: the daily reconciliation report, the baseline measures, the steering dashboard, the reporting baseline, the cross-source case count reconciliation, the measure refresh and the regulatory returns. DP-17 removes the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20 with it, and the target says reports come from rwb-reporting: Recovery has no data lake and no Power BI connection, and the extracts in JOB-15 run in rwb-reporting from its own projections. The seven rows still name a system that is no longer connected, so the delivery target of each row is undefined in the source.
evidence: Systems column of the seven rows reads 'Power BI, Data lake'. Architecture v5 line 707: 'The data lake and Power BI are not connected (INT-19 and INT-20 removed).' Lines 2701 and 2703: 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20)' becomes 'Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'. Line 2296: 'measures 01:30 (rwb-reporting, JOB-15, from its own projections: no data lake)'. DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; gap if the story needs lake data'.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-014 and the measure stories A11, A13 and A26
owner_role: Reporting lead of P9 rwb-reporting and the solution architect of P1 rwb-source-data
proposed: Keep the seven rows unchanged in v5. At story stage each read is taken from the rwb-reporting read model, built from events, and the extract is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-reporting (JOB-15). No feed to the data lake and no Power BI connection is built; if a story truly needs lake data it raises its own gap under DP-17.

title: Nine live features name the Quartz scheduler as their system while D-RCV-60 replaces it with Temporal Schedules
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-CWC-03, FEAT-CWC-11, FEAT-CWC-12, FEAT-CHO-06, FEAT-VAL-12, FEAT-LIT-03, FEAT-DVH-02, FEAT-DVH-03 and FEAT-DVH-06; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 and R6 (retired RWB-TE-007); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 2296 and 2974
section: Features rows listed above, column J
description: Nine live features hold the clock in the Quartz scheduler: the case state, the stage timers, the prescription dates, the treatment plan timers, the route flow timers, the litigation timers, the deviation pause, the prescription clock that keeps running during a deviation, and the resume after a deviation. R6 retires RWB-TE-007 (Quartz scheduler: replaced by Temporal Schedules in RWB-PLT-E1071) and DP-10 moves every Quartz job to a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow through the workflow kit; Arch v5 states that the ACE shared Quartz tables are no longer used. A timer is now a durable timer inside the workflow, not a job row, so the system named in the nine rows is retired.
evidence: Systems column of the nine rows includes 'Quartz scheduler'. R6: 'Retired | ... RWB-TE-007 (Quartz scheduler: replaced by Temporal Schedules in RWB-PLT-E1071) ... Dependencies on TE-007 point to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON.' Architecture v5 line 2296: 'The ACE shared Quartz tables are no longer used.' Line 2974: 'No shared Quartz tables: a Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow in the owning service'. DP-10: 'Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON'.
legacy_ref: RWB-TE-007 and the stories of the nine features
owner_role: Temporal platform lead and the solution architects of P3 rwb-case, S1 rwb-valuation, S4 rwb-litigation and S8 rwb-deviation
proposed: Keep the nine rows unchanged in v5. At story stage the clock is a Temporal Schedule or a durable timer in the owning service's workflow through RWB-PLT-E1071, and every dependency on TE-007 points to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON.

title: The workbook carries no wave column, and for 141 of the 378 features the service wave and the business-epic wave differ
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, Features column K and the By epic sheet; Template and Rules R5.6 W-MAP; Microservice Ownership Map v1, Services sheet
section: Features column P and the Read me Counts note; By epic sheet
description: The Feature List gives the business epic (E1 to E8) of every feature and no wave. Under D-RCV-60 a wave comes from two places: the service wave of Arch v5 and the business-epic wave of W-MAP (E1 wave 1; E2 and E3 wave 2; E4 and E5 wave 3; E6, E7 and E8 wave 4). Seventeen service-and-epic pairs disagree, covering 141 rows: P3 with E2 (26 rows), P7 with E2 (16), P4 with E8 (14), P6 with E2 (13), S5 with E4 (14), S6 with E6 (12), S8 with E7 (10), P8 with E4 (8), P6 with E4 (8), P9 with E2 (5), P10 with E2 (4), P10 with E8 (3), P9 with E8 (2), P5 with E2 (2), P10 with E3 (2), P8 with E6 (1) and P9 with E6 (1). In every one the epic wave is later than the service wave, so the service is available before the feature ships.
evidence: Features sheet has no wave column (14 columns, listed in row 4). Ownership Map v1 Services sheet wave column: P1 to P7, P9 and P10 wave 1; P8, S2, S5 and S8 wave 2; S1, S3, S4 and S6 wave 3; S7 and S9 wave 4. W-MAP: 'EP01 | 1; EP02, EP03 | 2; EP04, EP05 | 3; EP06, EP07, EP08 | 4'. Counted on the 378 feature rows of the copied sheet.
legacy_ref: None (no wave attribute in the source)
owner_role: Programme planner and the platform solution architect
proposed: Do not add a wave column in v5. Take the wave at story stage under R5.6: the W-MAP wave of the business epic, and a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service wave keeps the W-MAP wave. The Read me Counts note states the wave of each service so the reader can see both.

title: Two features govern feature flags in module P3 while the default ruling puts the flag store in the platform library
source: Recovery Workbench Feature List v4.xlsx, FEAT-CWC-26 and FEAT-CWC-29; Template and Rules R3 default ruling; Microservice Ownership Map v1, Tables and Rulings sheets
section: Features rows FEAT-CWC-26 and FEAT-CWC-29, columns B, E and J
description: FEAT-CWC-26 controls module release with dated feature flags and FEAT-CWC-29 accepts a queue placement that is disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists; both are P3 features. The R3 default ruling gives feature flags to the platform library, and the Ownership Map gives feature_flag and feature_flag_change to PLT with ruling ASM-A6-tables-7, which has rwb-integration serve the admin API against the library. The source treats the flag as part of the case and workflow module and says nothing about where the flag store lives, so the two rows do not say which service holds the flag.
evidence: FEAT-CWC-26: 'Control module release with dated feature flags', module P3, class Admin, story key C6. FEAT-CWC-29: 'Accept a queue placement from a model or an agent ... Disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists', module P3, story key N9. Template and Rules R3 default ruling table: 'Feature flags | Platform library'. Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: feature_flag and feature_flag_change owner PLT; Rulings sheet: 'Feature flags stay with the platform library (PLT, R-PREC default ruling); P2 serves the admin API against the library'.
owner_role: Platform library lead and the solution architect of P3 rwb-case
proposed: Keep both features in P3 as the administration capability that sets and reads a flag, with the Service column at P3 under the module rule. The flag table, its change history and the admin API are the platform library's (RWB-PLT-LIB), served through the rwb-integration admin API; no change to the workbook.
